speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for seeing me. To begin our evaluation of your painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg, can you tell me how long you have had this wound and if you noticed any redness or warmth spreading from the site?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum. The history of an initial "ant bite" (pathergy), rapid progression, combined with significant immunosuppression due to Crohn's disease and prior steroid use for uveitis, strongly suggests an inflammatory rather than infectious etiology.

REQUEST TEST: CBC, ESR, CRP, and Wound Culture.
REQUEST IMAGES: Clinical photograph of the leg lesion.
